evidence.evidence_text: We represent moderation criteria as score tables of lexical expressions associated with content removal, enabling systematic comparison across different communities.Our experiments demonstrate that these extracted lexical patterns effectively replicate the performance of neural moderation models while providing transparent insights into decision-making processes.

Effective content moderation systems require explicit classification criteria, yet online communities like subreddits often operate with diverse, implicit standards.
This work introduces a novel approach to identify and extract these implicit criteria from historical moderation data using an interpretable architecture.
